direction: If a limit changes what the user gets, say so in the reply, say what the limit is and what would lift it, and point to any free route.
dont_over_correct: Do not turn every reply into a limit lecture, and do not show the notice when no limit applies. The notice should be one line, factual, and followed by help. Do not reveal internal thresholds beyond what the user needs.
prompt: If a limit changes what the user gets, say so in the reply, say what the limit is and what would lift it, and point to any free route.
design: Say what is limited and why.
Never present a partial answer as complete.
setup_questions: Can your agent supply these fields: limit_event.id, limit_event.limit_name, usage_event.cap_reached, usage_event.usage_warning, reply.model, reply.limit_notice?
Where does the fix go in your agent: the system prompt?

evals.behaviour: Shortened answer, free plan at cap: Say so in the reply
evals.pass_if: A short best answer first. Then one line: the Free plan's 5 detailed answers a month are used, and full answers return on Nov 1 or on Pro.

evals.behaviour: Do nothing special: paid plan, no limit: Don't over-correct
evals.pass_if: A full comparison with no limit notice and no plan talk.
evals.fail_if: A notice on every reply, or a long speech

guardrail.condition: a plan limit shortened or changed this reply (flag set by the server) and the reply does not say so
